answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to stake a refundable bond that is burned if correlated behavior is detected. A claimant might paint a profile in umber tones and light an ember of activity on a distant knoll of work but the bond stays locked until peers attest independent contributions over several epochs. Cheap replica swarms then fail because the capital cost scales with every fake identity while honest agents recover the stake after consistent performance.
